examples.en: The letters are in the mailbox.
Take the knife out of the desk drawer.
An inspector has come to see us.

note: The plural «инспектора́» is stressed on the last syllable.
вверх = where to (upward); наверху́ = where (at the top).
The д is silent: pronounced «празник».

examples.en: She grew up in a small village.
We're going to the village to visit Grandma.
We're throwing a party for the kids.

note: A diminutive; masculine, but declines like «мама»: па́почки.

examples.en: He often comes to see us.
Come visit us over the weekend.

note: Arriving by transport; on foot it is «приходи́ть».

examples.en: He's still very weak after his illness.
A light wind was blowing through the window.
In the fairy tale, an evil dragon kidnapped the princess.
The girl wants to be a princess.
They are putting pressure on him.
We will build a bridge across the river.
Call a taxi, it's already late.

note: Indeclinable: на такси́, из такси́.

examples.en: It's no big deal that you were late.

note: «Не беда» means «no problem».

examples.en: He writes with his left hand.
My house is on the left side of the street.
The soldiers fought to the end.
He loves his mommy very much.

note: An affectionate diminutive of ма́ма.

examples.en: He threatened us with a knife.

note: Takes the dative: угрожа́ть кому́-то. Not to be confused with гроза́ (thunderstorm).

examples.en: There is a curse on him.
The old woman hurled a curse after us.
A big truck was driving in front of us.
Trucks are not allowed in here.
There is a new sheriff in town.
From here there is a magnificent view of the sea.
She is my colleague at work.

note: Used for both men and women; declines like «мама»: колле́ги.

examples.en: There's no need to apologize, everything is fine.

note: Takes «перед» + instrumental: «перед ма́мой».

examples.en: We once lived in a village.
You used to love this song.

note: Can refer to the past («once») or the future («someday»).
наверху́ = where (up there); наве́рх = where to (up).

examples.en: That was in the nineteenth century.

note: The stress moves in the plural: ве́ка, but века́.

examples.en: We continue the fight for freedom.

note: Not to be confused with за́втра (tomorrow).

examples.en: He can barely stand on his feet.
We got off at the next station.
Where is the nearest subway station?

note: A railway station (the building) is «вокза́л».

examples.en: The police established the identity of the victim.
Turn off the TV, it's time to sleep.
We watch the news on TV.

note: «Телеви́зор» is the set; broadcasting is «телеви́дение».
The plural is коле́ни, not «колена».

examples.en: An hour later he came back.

note: Takes the accusative: «спустя́ год» - a year later.

examples.en: Add a little salt to the soup.
There was an attack on the bank at night.
He was injured in the attack.
He introduced his fiancée to his parents.
The bride was wearing a white dress.

note: A longer journey; a short trip is «пое́здка».

examples.en: I quickly got used to the new city.

examples.ru: Она никак не может [привы́кнуть] к холоду.
examples.en: She just can't get used to the cold.

note: Takes «к» + dative: «привы́кнуть к го́роду».

examples.en: It was very dark in the room.
Open the door and come in.

note: внутрь = where to (inward); внутри́ = where (inside).

examples.en: At night we heard a gunshot.
The worker opened the manhole and climbed down.
In this case it doesn't matter.

note: Bookish: «в да́нный моме́нт» - at the moment.

examples.en: I'm meeting a friend at the station.
We often run into him in the park.

note: Also means to welcome arriving people: «встреча́ть госте́й».

examples.en: The trees bend in the wind.

note: The «е» drops out: gen. ве́тра.

examples.en: We are on board the plane.

note: «На борту́» means on board a ship or plane.

examples.en: A ghost lives in this house.
She is reading a fashion magazine.
Write this in the visitors' log.

note: A magazine; a newspaper is «газе́та».

examples.en: A bird is sitting on the branch.
Birds come back in the spring.
The dog ran away from home.
He ran away from the police.

examples.ru: Он [влюби́лся] в неё с первого взгляда.
examples.en: He fell in love with her at first sight.
They fell in love with each other.

note: Takes «в» + accusative; short form: влюблён, влюблена́.

examples.en: He rarely shows up at work.
He put the keys in his pocket.
I have no money in my pocket.
He has a great aptitude for languages.
It's an ability that needs to be developed.
He locked the door with a key.
She was locked in a room.
The prosecutor is demanding an arrest.
This job brings in a good income.

note: приноси́ть - to bring here; относи́ть - to take away.
Colloquial intensifier, like «damn».

examples.en: He graduated from the university last year.
I have a theory of my own.
We scheduled a meeting for Friday.

note: The post is in the instrumental: «назна́чить дире́ктором».

examples.en: Sorry, I dialed the wrong number.
You'll be wrong if you believe him.

note: The wrong thing is in the instrumental: «ошибиться номером».

examples.en: I need to rest after work.
The city's mayor opened the new bridge.
In his younger years he loved to travel.

note: Bookish; the everyday word is «молодо́й».

examples.en: The world is not what it seemed to be.

note: Bookish; mostly used in the short forms: такова́.

examples.en: This strange creature lives in the forest.
All living beings want to live.
We are looking for a suitable place.
This is not the right time for jokes.
He earned a lot of money.
I can't earn enough for a car.
Without a doubt, he is right.
The machine tool needs a new part.

note: Colloquial; very positive, like «great».

examples.en: He reminds me of my father.
She always reminds me about the meeting.

note: The pattern is «напомина́ть кому́ о чём»: to remind someone of something.

examples.en: The children are playing in the yard.
He served at the king's court.

note: Usually a yard; a palace is «дворе́ц».

examples.en: The street is full of people.
The fridge is full of food.

note: Colloquial; takes the genitive: «по́лно наро́ду».

examples.en: We'll move on to another topic.

meanings: to get to, to reach (on foot)
to dawn on, to sink in
note: Takes «до» + genitive: «дойти́ до реки́».
Also figurative: «золоты́е ру́ки» - a skilled craftsman.

examples.en: I'm going to the post office to send a letter.
He works at the post office.

note: Also e-mail: «электро́нная по́чта».

forms: comp. зле́е; short: зол, зла, зло
note: The short form зол, зла means angry: «она́ зла на меня́».

examples.en: He is being tried under the theft article of the criminal code.
She is like an angel, kind and sweet.
A full moon was shining at night.
They were looking at the moon.

note: The moon is «луна́»; «ме́сяц» means a calendar month.

examples.en: I'm in a good mood today.
He is in a bad mood.

related.en: to tune, to set; to put in a mood

examples.en: Can you confirm what I said?
It's nine o'clock in the morning now.
There are nine pupils in the class.
It makes me laugh when he talks like that.
He has a deep wound on his leg.
The children are playing with a ball.
My younger brother is still in school.
He is the youngest of three sons.
We like to relax in nature.
It has already become the norm.

note: «По-англи́йски» means in English.

examples.en: She poured water into a glass.
He works at a large firm.
We caught a crayfish in the river.
Don't forget to take an umbrella.
The train arrived at the station on time.

note: Bookish or official; in everyday speech «прие́хать».

examples.en: I'm very grateful to you for your help.
We are grateful to you for your support.

note: Dative for the person, «за» + accusative for the reason.
Colloquially, «маши́на» is more common.
Written as one word.
Colloquial exclamation: «Кошма́р!» - How awful!

examples.en: He reminded her of the debt.

note: The pattern is «напо́мнить кому́ о чём»: to remind someone of something.
«On Friday» is «в пя́тницу» (accusative).

examples.en: He is preparing for an exam.
We are getting ready for a trip.

note: Takes «к» + dative: «гото́виться к экза́мену».

meanings: but then, on the other hand

examples.en: It's noisy here, but it's cheap.
He's not rich, but he's kind.

note: Not «therefore» - that is «поэ́тому».
Takes the instrumental: «наслажда́ться жи́знью».

examples.en: She laid her head on his shoulders.

note: The stress shifts: плечо́, pl. пле́чи.

examples.en: My phone can't get a signal.
The fisherman cast the net into the water.
What good is that to you?

note: «В по́льзу кого́» - in favor of someone.
Plural only.

examples.en: I spent all my money in a week.
I don't want to waste time for nothing.
According to the law, this is forbidden.

note: Takes the dative: «согла́сно зако́ну».

examples.en: He looked at her with horror.

note: Colloquial: «Како́й у́жас!» - How awful!

examples.en: The room is clean and quiet.
Here is the women's locker room.

note: «Жена́» means wife; «woman» is «же́нщина».
Takes the genitive: «вне зако́на», «вне игры́».

examples.en: Put on your pants, it's cold.

note: Plural only.

examples.en: For dinner there will be meat with potatoes.

note: Indeclinable; colloquial.
Followed by the genitive plural: «два́дцать лет».

examples.en: We don't have internet at home.
I found this on the Internet.

note: Russian says «in» the Internet: «в интерне́те», not «на».

examples.en: The car got stuck in the mud.
We got stuck in the elevator.
This is a new phone model.
Let's go up, you can see better from there.
He ran upstairs for the keys.

note: наве́рх = where to (up); наверху́ = where (up there).

examples.en: They broke up a year ago.

examples.ru: Я не могу [расста́ться] с этой книгой.
examples.en: I can't part with this book.

note: Takes «с» + instrumental: «расста́ться с дру́гом».

examples.en: The children are playing in the garden.
He takes his daughter to kindergarten.
A hundred meters are left to the house.

note: Stressed on the first syllable: «ме́тр»; the subway is «метро́».

examples.en: The elevator isn't working, we're taking the stairs.
Bring the ladder, we need to change a light bulb.
I'll take the kids to school.
I'll work a little and then go.
We need to work on our mistakes.

note: The prefix «по-» means «for a while»: «порабо́тать час».

examples.en: It's not a problem, it's nothing.

note: Colloquial.

examples.en: We are not alone in the universe.
He kissed her on the cheek.

note: Colloquial; a friendly form of address.
The thing preferred is accusative, the other is dative: «предпочита́ть чай ко́фе».

examples.en: An old cannon stands in the square.
She has a very nice style of dress.

note: Masculine, ends in a soft sign: gen. сти́ля.

examples.en: The bird is sitting in the cage.
He was kidnapped right off the street.

note: Usually about people; ordinary theft is «укра́сть».

examples.en: There is fresh bread on the table.
Let's go out into the fresh air.

note: Not «frequent» - that is «ча́стый».

examples.en: He sold his soul to the devil.
What the hell are you doing here?
He looked everywhere for his keys.
My patience has reached its limit.
That is outside the city limits.
Don't worry, everything will be fine.
She is always nervous before an exam.
The shop owner himself stands behind the counter.
Who is the owner of this car?

note: The first «о» is pronounced like «а»: [малако́].
Colloquial.

examples.en: The policeman shot the thief dead.
He was shot dead in the building entrance.
The fingerprints are a perfect match.
The bathroom is at the end of the hall.
She is in the bathroom now.

note: «Ва́нная» is the room; «ва́нна» is the tub.
Also an adjective: «выходно́й день» - a day off.

examples.en: Your watch is five minutes fast.
This series has been running for five years.

note: «Сериа́л» is the whole show; «се́рия» is one episode.

examples.en: I'll stay at Grandma's for a week.

note: The prefix «по-» means «for a while».

examples.en: Who is to blame for this accident?

note: Takes the instrumental: «притворя́ться больны́м».

examples.en: I don't like talking about politics.
Wait, I'll come down in a moment.
The plane descended below the clouds.
The council approves the new plan.

note: Also a form of address: «това́рищ майо́р» - Comrade Major.
